hints: Focus on two things at once here, how many moles of gas each formula unit makes, and how heavy each formula unit is.
Write the four decomposition equations and notice that each carbonate gives 1 mole of gas while each nitrate gives 2.5 moles of gas per mole of solid.
For equal masses, divide moles of gas by Mr to get gas per gram, then see which combination of small Mr and large gas moles wins.
walkthrough:
**Write the decomposition equations**

Think of it simply, heating splits the solid and lets the gas escape. Count the gas molecules made from one formula unit.

$$\text{CaCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{CaO} + \text{CO}_2$$
$$\text{BaCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{BaO} + \text{CO}_2$$
$$2\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CaO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$
$$2\text{Ba(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{BaO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

**Count gas moles per mole of solid**

Each carbonate gives 1 mol of gas. Each nitrate gives 2.5 mol of gas per mol, because $2 + 0.5 = 2.5$ from $2\text{NO}_2 + \tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2$.

$$\text{carbonates: 1 mol gas per mol solid}$$
$$\text{nitrates: 2.5 mol gas per mol solid}$$

**Remember equal mass means fewer moles of heavy compounds**

Volume of gas under same conditions is proportional to moles of gas. For a fixed mass $m$:
$$n(\text{gas}) = \frac{m}{M_r(\text{solid})} \times \text{gas moles per mol}$$

**Compare Mr values**

Calcium compounds are much lighter than barium compounds, so the same mass contains many more moles. Approximate $M_r$ values:
$$M_r(\text{CaCO}_3) \approx 100, \quad M_r(\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2) \approx 164$$
$$M_r(\text{BaCO}_3) \approx 197, \quad M_r(\text{Ba(NO}_3)_2) \approx 261$$

**Combine both effects to find the winner**

Nitrates make more gas than carbonates, and calcium salts make more moles than barium salts. Calcium nitrate has both advantages.

$$\text{CaCO}_3: 1/100 = 0.0100$$
$$\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2: 2.5/164 \approx 0.0152$$
$$\text{BaCO}_3: 1/197 \approx 0.0051$$
$$\text{Ba(NO}_3)_2: 2.5/261 \approx 0.0096$$
Calcium nitrate gives the largest moles, and therefore the largest volume, of gas per gram.

options.A: CaCO3 gives only 1 mol of CO2 per mol. Although its Mr is the smallest at about 100, 1 divided by 100 is still less than 2.5 divided by 164 for calcium nitrate.
options.B: Ca(NO3)2 gives 2.5 mol of gas (2NO2 + 0.5O2) per mol and has a relatively low Mr of about 164. This combination of high gas stoichiometry and low Mr gives the greatest moles of gas per gram, so the greatest volume.
options.C: BaCO3 is doubly disadvantaged. It gives only 1 mol of gas per mol and has a large Mr of about 197 due to heavy Ba. It gives the smallest volume, not the largest.
options.D: Ba(NO3)2 does give 2.5 mol of gas per mol, but its Mr of about 261 is very large. Equal mass therefore contains far fewer moles than the calcium nitrate sample, so it produces less gas. A common trap is to look only at gas stoichiometry and forget Mr.
